about: How users who innovate for their own needs come to found firms, often without intending to, after others see and ask for their product.

candidates.label: Accidental user entrepreneur
candidates.definition: A user who innovated for their own use and founded a firm without having set out to start one; the venture emerges rather than being planned.
candidates.applies_when: The founder built something for themselves and only later, without a plan to start a firm, turned it into a business.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The founder set out to start a business and then looked for an idea.

candidates.label: Requests from people who see the product
candidates.definition: Others see the user's product in use and ask for one, which first shows there is demand.
candidates.applies_when: The founder says people saw what they had made and asked to buy or have one.
candidates.does_not_apply_when: The founder went looking for customers through planned market research.

candidates.label: Own unmet need as a user
candidates.definition: The innovation starts from a need the founder had as a user that existing products did not meet.
candidates.applies_when: The founder made the product first to solve their own problem.

candidates.label: Sharing in a user community
candidates.definition: Users share and improve ideas in a community, which spreads the innovation and reveals wider interest.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes showing, sharing or co-developing the product with fellow users or enthusiasts.

candidates.label: Enjoyment of the activity
candidates.definition: Users who enjoy the activity are more likely to keep innovating and to drift into founding.
candidates.applies_when: The founder says they did it because they loved the activity or hobby.

candidates.label: Low opportunity cost
candidates.definition: Founding is more likely when the user gives up little by starting the firm.
candidates.applies_when: The founder mentions having little to lose, such as being between jobs or a student.

candidates.label: Small niche market
candidates.definition: User entrepreneurship is more likely in niche markets that established firms ignore.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes a small or specialised market large firms did not serve.

candidates.label: New or turbulent market
candidates.definition: User entrepreneurship is more likely in young or fast-changing markets where needs are not yet understood.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes an emerging or fast-changing market.

candidates.label: Privileged knowledge from use
candidates.definition: Using a product gives users knowledge of needs and solutions that producers lack, which positions them to found firms.
candidates.applies_when: The founder says their idea came from knowledge gained by using such products themselves.

candidates.label: Did not expect to start a company
candidates.definition: Founders say in retrospect that they never expected their product to become a company.
candidates.applies_when: The founder states they had not planned or expected to found a firm.

candidates.label: Demand turns a hobby into a venture
candidates.definition: Recognising demand from others turns a personal project into a commercial opportunity and starts the venture.
candidates.applies_when: The founder describes the point where outside demand made them treat the project as a business.
